title: Typed element model: keep field values of a type the model has no form for (string strokeWidth) as upstream's restore does
description:
ex-108 restores each library item's elements with upstream's restoreElements, then reads each restored object with Element::from_map. Upstream's restore copies a truthy strokeWidth as it is, so a string "3" survives and the element loads; the typed model reads numbers only, so the port drops the element. In the catalogue that loses the 24 lines of aarondiel/logic-gates. ex-114's round-trip acceptance still passes after the drop, so this task tracks it. The same rule applies to scenes read through restore. M1 cannot close while this data loss remains.

Evidence:
- packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts:459 (strokeWidth: element.strokeWidth || DEFAULT_ELEMENT_PROPS.strokeWidth keeps the string "3") at the pinned commit
- fixtures/libraries: aarondiel/logic-gates holds 24 lines whose strokeWidth is the string "3"
- crates/excali-core/src/library.rs module docs (the two differences from upstream; Element::from_map rejects the object and restore drops the element)
- crates/excali-core/src/library.rs LibraryItem::from_map/to_map (values without a typed form written back as read) as the pattern
- site/content/architecture/file-format.md (library section, 'Two differences from upstream')
- site/content/decisions/adr-008-crate-boundaries.md (tracked exceptions)
acceptance_criteria: An element whose restored object has a known field holding a value of another JSON type than the model's (strokeWidth "3", a non-string fillStyle value, ...) is kept, not dropped, and written back as read until the field is changed, the way LibraryItem keeps an odd id or created: aarondiel/logic-gates parses to upstream's 24 lines and its serialized parse hashes to the output_sha256 in crates/excali-core/tests/fixtures/library.json, and crates/excali-core/tests/library.rs drops its logic-gates special case and elements_the_typed_model_cannot_read_are_dropped becomes a keep-as-read test against an upstream golden.
close_reason: Typed element model keeps restored field values of another JSON type (string strokeWidth) and writes them back as read; PR #52

title: Restore: legacy arrow binding migration (bindings without mode) through RestoreEnv::migrate_legacy_binding
description:
ex-104 ports restoreElement in excali-core, but the legacy binding migration needs shapes, bounds and hit testing that live in excali-editor above excali-core. Restore asks RestoreEnv::migrate_legacy_binding; its default answer (None) drops the binding, so legacy files lose arrow bindings on load until this lands. M1 cannot close while that data loss remains.

Evidence:
- packages/excalidraw/data/restore.ts:347-418 (binding schema v1 to v2 migration) at the pinned commit
- packages/element/src/collision.ts:829 (isPointInElement), packages/element/src/utils.ts:810 (projectFixedPointOntoDiagonal), packages/element/src/binding.ts:2196 (calculateFixedPointForNonElbowArrowBinding)
- crates/excali-core/src/restore/element.rs (RestoreEnv::migrate_legacy_binding; the default answer None drops the binding)
- site/content/decisions/adr-008-crate-boundaries.md (tracked exceptions)
acceptance_criteria: An arrow binding saved without mode whose target exists is kept with upstream's mode and fixedPoint, not dropped: excali-editor implements RestoreEnv::migrate_legacy_binding (LinearElementEditor.getPointAtIndexGlobalCoordinates, isPointInElement, projectFixedPointOntoDiagonal, calculateFixedPointForNonElbowArrowBinding at DEFAULT_ZOOM), and every restore-element.json case with a geometry field matches upstream's restoreElement result with the default environment (no fixture answer injected).

title: Attribution gate self-test in CI: a planted attribution line must fail the gate
description:

Evidence:
- site/content/plan/phases.md Milestone M0 and ex-m0 acceptance: "CI rejects a planted attribution line"
- .github/workflows/gates.yml: the attribution job runs the gate on the repo's own clean tree and history only; no job plants a violation (read 2026-09-28)
- scripts/gates/: no test for attribution.py exists (test_version.py and test_workspace.py only; read 2026-09-28)
- Local run 2026-09-28 in a fresh clone: attribution.py files --all exit 1 on a planted tool-attribution line (R2, R4); attribution.py history exit 1 on a commit-tree commit with a Co-Authored-By trailer (R1, R3, R4)
acceptance_criteria: scripts/gates/test_attribution.py builds a scratch git repo in a temp dir and plants, one at a time: a tool-attribution line in a tracked file, a Co-Authored-By trailer in a commit message (commit-tree, no hooks involved), a zero-width character, and a non-human author; each case asserts `attribution.py files --all` or `attribution.py history` exits non-zero with the rule id, and a clean control case exits 0. The gates workflow runs it on every PR and on main, and the M0 note links a green run in which the planted cases were rejected. Nothing planted is ever committed to or pushed from this repository.
close_reason: Attribution gate self-test plants violations in a scratch repo and runs in the gates workflow; green in CI on PR #14

title: Freedraw background fill: port getFreedrawFillCurvePoints and the loop fill curve of generateElementShape
description:
M2 check of 2026-09-28: the freedraw stroke path matches upstream byte for byte, but the rough.js background fill upstream draws under a looped freedraw is not ported, so freedraw has no fill-style parity at all.

Evidence:
- packages/element/src/shape.ts:244-253 (generateRoughOptions freedraw: fillStyle and fill only for loops), 580-581 (getFreedrawFillCurvePoints), 976-994 (freedraw shapes [background curve, stroke path]) at the pinned commit 438d898
- M2 check 2026-09-28: goldens/elements-freedraw.json has 14 cases whose shapes are ['rough', 'svgPath']; no Rust test reads a freedraw rough shape (crates/excali-scene/tests/freedraw_path.rs compares only the svgPath) and grep for getFreedrawFillCurvePoints / a freedraw fill builder over crates/ finds nothing; excali-scene's generate_element_shape returns NotABoxShape for freedraw
acceptance_criteria: excali-scene builds a freedraw element's shapes as upstream's ShapeCache.generateElementShape does (packages/element/src/shape.ts:976-994): when isPathALoop(points), first a rough.js curve over getFreedrawFillCurvePoints(element) = simplify(points, 0.75) (shape.ts:580-581) with generateRoughOptions(element, false, isDarkMode) and stroke "none", then the svgPath stroke; no fill shape otherwise. A test compares the rough shape (shapes[0]) of every looped case of goldens/elements-freedraw.json (loop-sw*, loop-pressure, loop-streamline0.2, loop-constant-sw*, loop-fill-hachure/cross-hatch/zigzag/solid/constant, loop-transparent) op by op, and asserts the non-loop cases have exactly one shape, the svgPath.
